perOption.reason: 'Sweeping statements have been made about...' — present perfect passive (have been + p.p.); subject 'statements' is the receiver of 'make'. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (B)
perOption.reason: 'It has been said that ... , and that ...' — extraposed-it with passive reporting verb; underlined 'that' introduces the first noun clause and is paralleled by the second 'and that'. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (C)
perOption.reason: 'a child who was dressed in his best clothes and whose mother stressed...' — two coordinated relative clauses share the antecedent 'a child'; possessive relative 'whose' is required before 'mother'. The parallel start point ('who was...' and 'whose mother...') is a tempting checkpoint but both clauses attach to the same antecedent, so it is correct.

perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'by the end of the hour the child would have forgetting his clothes' — modal perfect requires 'would have + past participle' → 'would have forgotten'. No alternative parse rescues it: not a causative 'have + O + -ing' (word order is 'have forgetting his clothes'), and a progressive would need 'would have been forgetting'. The coordinated 'and would be acting' confirms the modal-perfect frame. Ungrammatical.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: 'might be very noisy while playing cowboys' — elliptical adverbial clause 'while (he is) playing'; implicit subject matches the main-clause subject 'the child'. Grammatical.
